approach: Extend `check_defined_terms` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs so the names it requires a `Term <name>:` definition for are STRUCTURAL_TERMS plus a new constant `AMBIGUOUS_NAMES: [&str; 1] = ["Hermes"]`. A private `named_term(word)` replaces `structural_term`. Structural terms keep the singular, plural and possessive forms, and an ambiguous name matches as a whole word or its possessive. The plain-prose filter (`plain_request_prose`), the skipped generated lines, `defined_terms` and the three-word rule are reused unchanged. The error text is reworded to cover ambiguous names and still ends with the repair `Term Hermes: <meaning>`. A unit test parses docs/ontology.toml with the existing `crate::mirrors::parse_ontology` and fails if any listed name is not a term there, so the list cannot drift from the shared vocabulary. The doc comment of `check_defined_terms` is rewritten (root cause, the three jobs, 2 of 3, expected 2%, and no claim that Hermes is uncovered). The `check_outcome_state` doc line "no check catches the second" is corrected. Corpus: the 0wtc request becomes a named constant, the two replay tests assert that check_defined_terms now refuses it (2 of 3) and accepts it once a `Term Hermes:` line is added, and new cases cover the input forms. CHANGELOG.md gets a new entry at the top of Added (old entries stay as history). docs/decisions.md gets an appended D165 (the log is append-only) that amends D164. Root cause named in all three places: readings are not checked against the outcome the user observes, so ambiguous names stay undefined.

decisions.choice: Add `AMBIGUOUS_NAMES` beside STRUCTURAL_TERMS and run both through the one function `named_term`; do not add a second check.
decisions.reason: The need is the same: the request uses a word whose meaning the reading must state before work builds on it. The plain-prose filter, the generated-line skips, the `Term x:` definition rule and the step line in `refusing_check` already exist and are tested. The fault starts in the one gate that turns wording into a reading. One list-driven function covers the class (any recorded ambiguous name), not just Hermes.

rejected.why: It would duplicate the prose filter and definition parsing. `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` and the step-order tests would need new entries, for no gain.

rejected.option: Read every `[[term]]` name from docs/ontology.toml at run time and refuse on any of them
rejected.why: The ontology holds names like `job`, `planning` and `landed` that appear in most requests, so refusals would be very frequent. The file is not in the snapshot a reader sees, and the request puts wiring the ontology into agent prompts out of scope. A small constant plus a sync test keeps the list to terms that caused a reading misread.
The misread is the bare name. A request that says 'Hermes' alone (the Orchestration god) is the other sense and needs the same definition.

decisions.choice: Store the name in its ontology case (`"Hermes"`) and compare it lowercase, returning the canonical string, so the error says `Term Hermes:`. Structural terms stay lowercase. Ambiguous names get no plural stem, only the exact word and the `'s` possessive.
decisions.reason: The brief asks for the repair text `Term Hermes: <meaning of at least three words>`. `defined_terms` already lowercases assumptions, so `term hermes:` and `Term Hermes:` both define it. A plural stem would make `hermess` a use, which is not a word.

rejected.option: Store the name lowercase like the structural terms
rejected.why: The error would say `Term hermes:`, which does not match the ontology name or the requested repair text, and the sync test could not compare it with the `[[term]]` name directly.

decisions.choice: Check the list against the ontology with a unit test in reading.rs, using the existing `crate::mirrors::parse_ontology` and `include_str!("../../../docs/ontology.toml")`, with a negative control.
decisions.reason: This is enforced by mechanism, not prose, and needs no new dependency. `include_str!` makes a moved or renamed ontology fail the build. The control (a name not in the ontology is reported) shows the test can fail.

rejected.why: That file is a kept deliverable of 0wtc and the brief says it stays unchanged. The constant is private to athena-core.
It duplicates the parser and breaks on a reordered key.

demonstrations.method: A content test over the source text. It reads the `///` block above `pub fn check_defined_terms(` (the helper `defined_terms_doc()` exists at reading.rs:10791), and calls `check_defined_terms` on a Hermes request to read the error. The updated `defined_terms_refusal_is_declared_intended` keeps the old needles other than the share and requires `expected 2% of newly refused readings` in the doc.
demonstrations.observes: The doc contains `readings are not checked against the outcome the user observes`, the three job ids, `covers 2 of the 3 cited jobs` and `expected 2% of newly refused readings`, and does not contain `whose recorded request holds no word of the list`. The error contains `ambiguous name`, `Term Hermes:` and no newline, and still starts with `the reading was refused because`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the rewrite the doc comment still says the Hermes term is not covered and has no `expected 2%` text, and the error says only `structural term`, so the test's contains and does-not-contain assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `check_defined_terms` and the source text via `include_str!("reading.rs")` (the pattern used by `defined_terms_doc`, exists). No double. New test added in step 3; the declared-intended test is edited in step 3.

demonstrations.method: A content test that reads CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md with `include_str!` and checks the new entry and D165 for the needles. It also checks that the old wording the other tests need is still present.
demonstrations.observes: The whitespace-normalised changelog holds `readings are not checked against the outcome the user observes`, the ids 20261014-082328-g6vy, 20261014-174815-7bf8 and 20261017-173508-0wtc, and states that `check_outcome_state` covers 20261014-082328-g6vy while `check_defined_terms` covers 20261014-174815-7bf8 and 20261017-173508-0wtc. D165 holds `**Alternatives:**`, `**Provenance:**`, the same root-cause sentence, `amends D164` and `expected 2% of newly refused readings`. The existing `mirrors` decision-log checks (Provenance bullet, next id) accept D165.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the CHANGELOG entry and D165 the needles (root cause sentence, the three job ids, `check_outcome_state`, `check_defined_terms`, `covers 2 of the 3 cited jobs`) are not found.
demonstrations.seam: Production items: the two files themselves, included at compile time as in refusal_corpus.rs:541 and 618 (exist). The test is added in step 5. No double.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks the same way Athena does: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, with warnings treated as errors by the host (`-- -D warnings`). Because the run also calls `cargo test` for the whole workspace, it exercises every crate that reaches `check_reading_acceptance`.
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0 with no warning output. Also run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked` and `cargo test --locked`. The workspace test run covers athena-core (unit and refusal_corpus), athena-cli (ontology and mirrors tests, unchanged) and athena-context (briefs tests).
demonstrations.fails_without: A formatting error, a clippy warning (for example an unused `structural_term` left after the rename, or `dead_code` on `AMBIGUOUS_NAMES`) or a broken existing test fails the respective command.
demonstrations.seam: The cargo commands themselves; nothing to inject. The three commands are in the verifier's list.
